item.title: The U.S. debt tops a record-shattering $40 trillion. Yes, with a T
item.description: The federal debt reached $40 trillion as the government adds red ink at a rapid rate. That's leading nervous investors to demand higher interest rates — pushing up borrowing costs for everyone else.

item.title: Trump says U.S. and Canada reached deal to delay 50% U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports
item.description: President Trump said he was delaying the 50% U.S. tariffs on Canadian imports after the two countries reached a last-minute deal less than two hours before the sanctions were to go into effect.

item.title: Many recent grads say AI is making it harder to get a job. Economists aren't so sure
item.description: The unemployment rate for young adults with new degrees is higher than the rate for all workers, according to the New York Fed. Is AI the problem, or is it more complicated?

item.title: Living with nuns: Priced out of D.C., young women found low rent with unlikely roommates
item.description: For 10 years, a Catholic-run home offered young women an affordable place to live in the nation's capital as they studied and launched careers. Now, that community is saying goodbye.

item.title: The money investors borrow to trade in the U.S. stock market is at an all-time high
item.description: Money that investors borrow to trade in the stock market is called margin debt. This debt is now above $1.5 trillion, 50% higher than a year ago. Could this spell trouble for the U.S. economy?

item.title: Latest inflation report may give the Fed more time for its control efforts
item.description: Inflation cooled a bit last month. Gas and grocery prices dipped and the overall cost of living rose more slowly, giving the Federal Reserve some breathing room for inflation control efforts.

item.title: People are giving up their pets due to costs — and rehoming them is more expensive too
item.description: The cost of pet care is rising. Petflation is affecting more than the cost of food and care; it's also making it costlier to transport pets between shelters, the key to getting many animals adopted.

item.title: Inflation eases in July as gasoline and grocery prices fall
item.description: Consumer prices in July were up 3.4% from a year ago — a smaller annual increase than in May or June. The news makes it less likely the Fed will feel the need to raise interest rates in September.
item.content:encoded:
